measured_decisions.decision: Glyph-box occurrence granularity with exact-box coalescing
measured_decisions.reason: PDFium expands one ToUnicode glyph ('1' -> '1,0') into several scalars reporting one identical charbox; coalescing preserves the expansion without invented widths, while duplicates at distinct positions stay distinct (I02).

measured_decisions.decision: Physical geometry from pypdf metadata, UserUnit applied once
measured_decisions.reason: Measured: PdfDocument.get_size() rotates crop dims but ignores UserUnit (userunit-10 still reports 520x400), matching planning/architecture/COORDINATES.md; contract mandates metadata-based compensation.
Raw fidelity (I03); conservative normalization semantics are T12's contract; the declared 'scalar-whitespace-v1' setting is recorded but no transformation is applied here.

measured_decisions.decision: Render capability declared unavailable in the PDFium manifest
measured_decisions.reason: Render-scale compensation is not proven under this task; claiming it would overstate the manifest. T27/T28 own rendered-region work.

review_attention: F10/F11 are covered by in-test synthesized mechanisms (missing-ToUnicode passthrough; four-position duplicates) because those fixture families remain 'specified' in the catalog; committed fixture generation is requested from the fixture owner lane.
extract() performs per-character get_text_range/get_charbox API calls (bounded by MAX_CHARS_PER_PAGE=200000); fine for contract fixtures, and T29 supervision owns wall-time budgets.
PDFium UTF-16 code-unit indexing: supplementary-plane scalars are not asserted here (F14 territory).
limitations: No Linux execution claimed: this run is macOS arm64 under the frozen uv lock; cross-environment parity is T46 scope.
No render/OCR/structure capability is claimed by these manifests; only native_text (+ crop_metadata declaration for pypdf).
dependency_requests: Fixture owner (T05/T21 lane): generate committed F10/F11 fixture families using the established generator API.
T29: wrap these in-process adapters with the parent/child supervision, two-message backpressure acknowledgment and atomic partial-result contract.
